title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the 2020 Committee report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its commitment to improving safety, transparency, and accountability in AI deployments. It proposes new standards, regulatory frameworks, and partnerships with industry and academia to ensure responsible AI development and use across the public sector.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is laying out how it will monitor and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications to keep assessments fair, reliable, and free from cheating. This guidance was issued in response to a request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used in training and developing AI systems and evaluates the resulting legal and economic implications. It also offers recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with the benefits of AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to strengthen AI regulation, boost research and development, and ensure the technology is used safely and ethically. It emphasizes the need for international cooperation, investment in talent, and robust safeguards to protect citizens while fostering innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing artificial intelligence in relation to public standards. It also provides a set of frequently asked questions to clarify the committee’s role, expectations, and the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has written to the Science and Technology Committee to share its thoughts on how to govern artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the organisation’s views and recommendations for ensuring AI is developed and used safely, responsibly, and in line with public interest.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how AI technologies will change the regulation of medical products, aiming to embed the AI White Paper’s principles into current regulatory frameworks. It outlines steps to ensure safety, efficacy, and ethical use of AI-driven medical devices while maintaining compliance with existing medical product laws.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines how the organisation plans to lead in AI, aiming to be the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence entity in the world for its size. It sets a vision for using AI to enhance national security capabilities and maintain a cutting‑edge technological edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to harness artificial intelligence for efficiency, safety, and innovation, while also addressing potential risks and ensuring responsible deployment. It establishes guidance, support mechanisms, and regulatory measures to foster safe, ethical, and transparent use of AI across the transport sector.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: It reports on how copyright works are currently used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. The report outlines the progress made, identifies challenges, and discusses regulatory considerations for ensuring copyright compliance.
